translation_notes: Identity translation: `query_tpl % "GROUP_CONCAT"` splices the SPARQL AGGREGATE FUNCTION NAME into `(%s(DISTINCT ?z_) as ?z)` -- a syntax position, not a term. `s{ }`'s interpolation ({expr}) is legal only in TERM position and lowers to initBindings; there is no island for 'a keyword chosen by string formatting', the same limit already recorded for the sibling region test_agg_undef.py::template_tst in this same stratum.

the value is fixed ("GROUP_CONCAT") at this call site, but `query_tpl` is the same module-level template reused with a different aggregate name ("SUM") by the sibling test test_sum_distinct in the real file (not itself extracted as a region) -- so this is genuinely the parametrised idiom, not an incidental one-off string, even though only one instantiation is visible in this region.

minimal excerpt showing the limit: `query_tpl % "GROUP_CONCAT"` where `query_tpl` is `"SELECT ?x (MIN(?y_) as ?y) (%s(DISTINCT ?z_) as ?z) { VALUES (?x ?y_ ?z_) {...} } GROUP BY ?x ORDER BY ?x"` -- `s{ }` cannot even parse this text at transpile time, since `%s` is not valid SPARQL.
no fixture graph: `g = Graph()` is built empty inside the function, and all data comes from the query's own inline VALUES clause -- fixture.ttl is unused (see its header).

test_group_concat_distinct only asserts (no return, no mutated argument to compare); `return results` was appended identically to both original.py and translated.ldpy purely so run_pair has a value to diff (same pattern already used for sparql_literal's test_select_star_multiple_sub_select_star and this stratum's template_tst).
